# Training Optimization and Initialization

Also called: 3DGS Initialization Policy, 3D Gaussian Splatting Training, GauFRe

## Overview
This family defines the strategies for seeding the initial set of $N$ 3D Gaussian primitives and the iterative optimization process that adjusts their parameters to minimize the difference between rendered images and ground truth views. It sets itself apart from NeRF-based methods by optimizing explicit geometric and appearance attributes rather than neural network weights, offering significantly faster training and inference speeds [3761-3d-gaussian-splatting-training.md]. Unlike static initialization methods, it employs adaptive density control to dynamically manage the number and distribution of Gaussians during training [3761-3d-gaussian-splatting-training.md].

## Shared principles
All methods in this family optimize a set of $N$ 3D Gaussian primitives [3761-3d-gaussian-splatting-training.md]. Each primitive $i$ is defined by:
*   Position $\mathbf{p}_i \in \mathbb{R}^3$
*   Rotation $q_i \in \mathbb{R}^4$ (unit quaternion)
*   Scale $\mathbf{s}_i \in \mathbb{R}^3$
*   Opacity $\alpha_i \in [0, 1]$
*   Appearance parameters (e.g., spherical harmonic coefficients $h_i$) [3761-3d-gaussian-splatting-training.md]

The optimization minimizes a loss function $\mathcal{L}$ between rendered images and ground truth views, typically using the Adam optimizer [3761-3d-gaussian-splatting-training.md]. The rendering process involves projecting 3D Gaussians to 2D screen space, sorting by depth, and [alpha blending](#5750-alpha-blending.md) [3761-3d-gaussian-splatting-training.md].

## Subtopics

### [3DGS Initialization Policy](1398-3dgs-initialization-policy.md)
The 3DGS Initialization Policy defines the strategy for seeding the initial set of $N$ 3D Gaussian primitives before optimization begins. It addresses the problem of sparse or incorrect initial geometry, which can lead to poor convergence or artifacts in the final radiance field. Unlike dynamic densification strategies that spawn primitives during training based on view-space gradients, this policy acts once before optimization using the initial scene geometry or [random distribution](#13385-grouped-vs-interleaved-macro-distribution.md). It sets apart from standard [random initialization](#9657-gaussian-initialization-and-warm-up.md) by potentially incorporating specific opacity scaling laws derived from order-independent transparency (OTS) formulations [1398-3dgs-initialization-policy.md].

### [3D Gaussian Splatting Training](3761-3d-gaussian-splatting-training.md)
[3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS)](#1174-3d-gaussian-splatting-3dgs.md) Training is the iterative optimization process that adjusts the parameters of a set of 3D Gaussian primitives to minimize the difference between rendered images and ground truth views [3761-3d-gaussian-splatting-training.md]. It solves the problem of reconstructing photorealistic 3D scenes from 2D images without relying on neural network weights, instead optimizing explicit geometric and appearance attributes [3761-3d-gaussian-splatting-training.md]. It sets itself apart from NeRF-based methods by offering significantly faster training and inference speeds while achieving comparable image quality [3761-3d-gaussian-splatting-training.md]. Unlike static initialization methods, it employs adaptive density control to dynamically manage the number and distribution of Gaussians [3761-3d-gaussian-splatting-training.md].

### [GauFRe](7994-gaufre.md)
[GauFRe](#7994-gaufre.md) is a method for real-time dynamic novel view synthesis that represents dynamic scenes using [deformable 3D Gaussian](#16260-deformable-3d-gaussians.md) primitives [7994-gaufre.md]. It solves the problem of reconstructing non-rigid motion from monocular video by employing a [forward-warping deformation field](#15458-gaussian-deformation-field-gaufre.md), which explicitly models the temporal evolution of scene geometry [7994-gaufre.md]. Unlike backward-warping approaches common in NeRFs that require querying a canonical space, GauFRe predicts the deformed primitive system at a specific time directly, making it efficient for explicit primitive-based rendering [7994-gaufre.md]. It distinguishes itself by decoupling static and dynamic regions into separate Gaussian sets and applying exponential/normalization constraints to scale and rotation parameters for stable optimization [7994-gaufre.md].

### Training Optimization
#### definition
- Joint optimization of network weights, feature grids, and latent codes using the total training loss [S1].
#### parameter
- $\Theta_s$: Learnable parameters of [SDF](#1466-signed-distance-fields-sdf.md) model [S1].
- $\Theta_d$: Learnable parameters of [DDF](#9276-directed-distance-fields-ddf.md) model [S1].
- $M$: SDF and DDF feature grids, $M = (M_s, M_d)$ [S1].
- $M_s$: SDF feature grids, $M_s = \{M^s_i \mid i = xy, yz, zx\}$ [S1].
- $M_d$: DDF feature grids, $M_d = \{M^d_i \mid i = pxpy, \dots, rzrx\}$ [S1].
- $Z$: Set of latent codes for $J$ training shapes, $Z = \{z_i \mid i = 1\dots J\}$ [S1].
- $w_s, w_d, w_\sigma, w_{tv}, w_{ts}, w_l$: Weights for respective losses [S1].

## Background
The foundational 3D Gaussian [Splatting](#23-splatting.md) method was introduced by Kerbl et al. in 2023, establishing the explicit primitive-based rendering pipeline [3761-3d-gaussian-splatting-training.md]. The initialization policy utilizing opacity scaling laws was detailed in subsequent analyses of the 3DGS training dynamics [1398-3dgs-initialization-policy.md]. GauFRe extended this framework to dynamic scenes in 2024, introducing forward-warping deformation fields [7994-gaufre.md]. The "[Training Optimization](#6838-coarse-to-fine-sparse-volume-training.md)" variant referencing SDF/DFD grids originates from the FIRe method for inverse rendering [S1].
